textauszug: block on Borneo Island Amsterdam 1996-2000 Planning ideas The project is sited on part of Borneo Island in Amsterdam Port, in a very unusual situation at the tip of the island surrounded by water on three sides. The project is a low mass with projections and recesses. Functionally speaking the apartments form a huge collective space that invades the entire terrain. The bedrooms and other specialized facilities stick out like little towers above this space. Light penetrates from between the interstices the protruding volumes leave down towards the ground floor. The roof, the facade with most surface area, is a part-domestic, part-abstract landscape. From it the protruding volumes impart a small, almost rural, scale to the whole. The complex is a sculpted mass fashioned along the two coordinating axes X, the strict system of parallel concrete walls and same-size windows, and Y: the emergent volumes that move in a non-mechanical way above these. Notwithstanding the serried, repetitive character of the design, the complex is not just an expression of accretion, but possesses an internal unity. The built mass begins at the key moment of its junction with the adjacent mass and unfolds in a particular way as far as the end wall giving onto the three canals. This produces a great variety of dwelling possibilities controlled and made possible by the strict structural and constructional logic employed. On top of the hard logic of the walls sustaining the building, the facades are fine skins of varying thickness and permeability, and made of tropical wood with a hermetically sealed look handled according to the technologies typical of boat building. In a beautiful and special location, surrounded by the sea on three sides, the design seeks to be open, diffuse and of scant solidity. [From the competition statement, 1995]. Construction process and form The construction has involved a long process that has enabled us to define its features with precision. The wooden envelopes of treated Canadian cedar, albeit without surface protection, were resolved in the workshop by constructing a fragment of the facade at a scale of 1:1. This led to utilizing the wood as a massive element of the surface by resolving the small, one-off pieces, which produce thick, chunky sections in the wood, with slim aluminum contouring. The tension between the mass and the small, shiny aluminum elements forms the basis of the building’s expression. The building is basically faced in wood its situation, literally above the water, plus the fact that the client is also the owner of an important and technologically advanced wood factory, led to this choice but on top of that the building has to be anchored to the ground without reducing the pure expression of lightness, all of which led us to imagine its outer skin with a complexity in which the lightweight aspect, the omnipresent wood on the south facade, gradually diminishes until disappearing on the almost all-brick north facade. This monotone, regular and traditional facade sought to counterbalance the variegated group of single-family houses by different authors and with different shapes on the other side of the canal. Lightness and weight, wood and brick and their particular constructional and compositional systems make up a complementary system akin to a mandala which attempts to respond to both the aquatic, gaseous nature of the location and the need for anchorage, stability and protection called for by the housing.
